html:
Space Coast questions: will a Melbourne NDT job put you under SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410?

Brevard County mixes aircraft assembly, defense electronics, rocket hardware and marine work, so two NDT technicians living on the same street in Melbourne can be certified under different documents. These are the questions people on the Space Coast most often need answered. The national comparison sits in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

I am applying to an aircraft assembler near the airport. Which standard will apply?

Embraer assembles executive jets at Orlando Melbourne International Airport, and Northrop Grumman runs a large military aircraft engineering and manufacturing campus beside it. Inside an aircraft maker, the standard is whatever the company's written practice names, and you will learn it fastest by asking the Level 3 at interview. Among the machine shops, sheet-metal houses and processors supplying airframe programs, the usual answer is NAS 410, or EN 4179 for European customers, because the buyer writes it into the purchase-order quality clause and it flows down to every shop that tests the parts.

What about rocket and spacecraft hardware at the Cape?

North of Melbourne, launch providers and their contractors build and process vehicles at Kennedy Space Center, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and Merritt Island. Some of that hardware is fracture-critical metal on NASA programs. NASA-STD-5009C, approved in August 2023, requires that personnel doing standard or special NDE of fracture-critical hardware be qualified and certified Level II, at a minimum, in accordance with NAS 410; when a contract invokes that standard, the rule reaches the supplier holding the part. Commercial launch customers and defense programs set their own flow-downs. Ground support equipment, pressure systems and launch structures built to ASME and AWS codes are usually inspected by people certified under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A.

Avionics companies do little NDT, don't they?

Less than an airframe line, but not none. L3Harris has its headquarters in Melbourne and Collins Aerospace operates in the city. Electronics and antenna production leans on other inspection, yet housings, brackets, castings and the supplier parts behind them still get penetrant, ultrasonic and visual work. Defense contractors commonly see NAS 410 flowed down from the prime, since it replaced MIL-STD-410 on defense contracts in 1998.

I hold an SNT-TC-1A Level II from port or power work. Will it carry over?

Not by itself. Under both schemes your employer certifies you and the certification ends when you leave. A NAS 410 shop's Responsible Level 3 (RL3) reviews your training records, experience log and examination history and decides what to credit; an SNT-TC-1A certificate is useful evidence but does not meet a NAS 410 requirement alone. The common gap for people coming from Port Canaveral or Florida Power & Light outage work is formal training in penetrant and magnetic particle testing, which NAS 410 requires in greater depth and with documented outlines. Check where you stand against SNT-TC-1A eligibility first, then ask the RL3 what else they need.

What should a Brevard supplier fix before a Nadcap or prime audit?

Write the governing standard and revision on every certification. If you run aerospace and industrial programs side by side, keep them visibly separate. Decide when you will move a NAS 410 program to Revision 6, released in December 2025, and change the written practice, training material and examination banks together. Nadcap AC7114 auditors and customer auditors choose inspectors and trace each signature back to training, experience, examination and vision evidence. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation for your RL3 to approve, and our aerospace NDT consulting covers written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, plus procedures and Level I and II examinations.

What can Atlantis do for me on the Space Coast?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. You work through theory online at your own pace with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, practise in the Practical NDT simulator, and complete hands-on work and the practical examination at your employer's site under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Melbourne. Courses most relevant to Brevard work include penetrant testing training and ultrasonic testing training. Brevard companies needing inspection can ask Atlantis for UT, MT, PT and VT.

One limit Space Coast readers should know: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. Your employer's RL3 decides whether SNT-TC-1A-based training counts toward a NAS 410 certification, so ask before you enroll. The way NAS 410 programs are run is explained in NAS 410 explained.
